nodes.title: Invariant tensor powers
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, an R-module M and n≥0, TSymⁿ_R(M) is the submodule of TensorPower R n M fixed by every permutation of Fin n, acting by PiTensorProduct.reindex. It is an invariant submodule, not the symmetric-power quotient.
proofSteps: Intersect LinearMap.eqLocus(reindex σ,id) over permutations σ.
Membership is the family of fixed-point equations using Submodule.mem_iInf.
Diagonal pure tensors are fixed by reindex_tprod; restriction of tensor maps uses map_reindex.
acceptance: For a commutative ring R, an R-module M and n≥0, TSymⁿ_R(M) is the submodule of TensorPower R n M fixed by every permutation of Fin n, acting by PiTensorProduct.reindex. It is an invariant submodule, not the symmetric-power quotient.

sources.match: Invariant tensor notation and diagonal powers are used here; the invariant-submodule carrier is specified explicitly and checked against the pinned tensor API.

nodes.title: Shuffle multiplication and divided powers
nodes.statement: For tensors invariant under S_m and S_n, sum over (m,n)-shuffles to obtain TSym^m(M)×TSym^n(M)→TSym^(m+n)(M). It is associative and commutative; diagonal divided tensors satisfy v^[m]v^[n]=binom(m+n,m)v^[m+n] and v^n=n!v^[n].
proofSteps: Partition permutations into shuffle cosets.
Use the three-block shuffle bijection for associativity and block exchange for commutativity.
Count shuffle cosets on diagonal tensors.

nodes.title: Multigrading of invariant tensors
nodes.statement: For a finite family of finitely generated projective R-modules Mσ and M=⊕σ Mσ, there is a natural multigraded isomorphism TSym^k(M)≃⊕_{|α|=k}⊗σ TSym^{α(σ)}(Mσ). No such isomorphism for arbitrary nonflat summands is asserted.

Use orbit sums of the word basis to identify each multidegree with the tensor product of the component invariant modules.
The local map is the canonical shuffle map, hence the isomorphisms glue; flatness/local freeness is used when identifying invariants after tensoring.

nodes.title: Universal vector extension of the dual
nodes.statement: For an abelian scheme A/S in the source noetherian setting, A♮ represents rigidified invertible sheaves L on A_T with integrable T-relative connection satisfying the theorem of the square. The forgetful map p:A♮→A∨ has vector kernel ω_A and universal bundle P♮=(id_A×p)^*P with universal connection. Thus A♮ is the extension of A∨, not A.
proofSteps: Form the fppf moduli functor of pairs (L,∇) with the rigidification.
The representing smooth group and universal connection require the Mazur–Messing/Laumon representability input recorded as a gap.
Forget ∇ to map to A∨; the kernel is the additive vector group of invariant one-forms.

The forgetful map p:A♮→A∨ has vector kernel ω_A and universal bundle P♮=(id_A×p)^*P with universal connection. Thus A♮ is the extension of A∨, not A.

nodes.title: Moments of a formal smooth group
nodes.statement: For a separated smooth commutative group G/S of finite presentation, with closed unit section e, its unit ideal J has J^n/J^(n+1)≃Sym^n(ω_G). Iterating the coproduct and projecting each factor O_G/J²→ω_G gives mom_n:O_G/J^(n+1)→⊕_{b≤n}TSym^b(ω_G), compatible with truncation; their inverse limit lands in degree completion. Over a Q-algebra the moment maps are isomorphisms.
proofSteps: Import formal infinitesimal thickenings from SF.4; the formal functor is the filtered union of the thickenings while its coordinate ring is an inverse limit.
Use smoothness for the conormal associated-graded comparison.

Cocommutativity makes the iterated projection invariant. On associated gradeds use the canonical symmetrization Sym^b(ω_G)→TSym^b(ω_G): a monomial of multiplicities α has coefficient ∏σ α(σ)! in the orbit-sum basis. For a diagonal power this coefficient is b!. All these coefficients are invertible over a Q-algebra.
acceptance: For a separated smooth commutative group G/S of finite presentation, with closed unit section e, its unit ideal J has J^n/J^(n+1)≃Sym^n(ω_G). Iterating the coproduct and projecting each factor O_G/J²→ω_G gives mom_n:O_G/J^(n+1)→⊕_{b≤n}TSym^b(ω_G), compatible with truncation; their inverse limit lands in degree completion. Over a Q-algebra the moment maps are isomorphisms.

sources.match: Iterated coproduct and the split first neighborhood yield compatible moments. The symmetrization is invertible over a Q-algebra; completion uses the explicitly chosen degree topology.

nodes.title: Period-coordinate trivializations
nodes.statement: For a polarized abelian scheme A→S of relative dimension g over a smooth irreducible quasi-projective complex variety S, choose connected simply connected U⊂S^an and a symplectic lattice frame of polarization type D=diag(d₁,…,d_g). nodes.title: Normality and quotient induction
nodes.statement: Let M=Γ\X⁺ be a connected Kuga mixed Shimura variety with uniformization u, Δ=graph(u), and Z an irreducible analytic component of B∩Δ where B=Z^Zar. Replace the ambient datum (P,X⁺) by the smallest Kuga subdatum containing pr_X⁺Z. For the purpose of proving the dimension inequality one may replace (B,Z) by a very general pair in its Hilbert family, with no larger dimension defect and the same bi-algebraic closure, so that its rational stabilizer H is normal in P. The vector part V∩H is a G=P/V module and the reductive part acts trivially on V/(V∩H). Quotient by H and compare generic fibre dimensions to obtain the Ax–Schanuel inequality. nodes.title: The fibre-power dimension induction
nodes.statement: Let A→S be an abelian scheme over an irreducible complex quasi-projective variety, and X⊂A closed irreducible and dominant, with geometrically irreducible generic fibre, positive relative dimension, generating fibres and finite geometric generic stabilizer. For part(ii), obtain a section only after a finite cover and shrinking; translate X so that it contains zero. Its difference image contains X^[m], has dimension at most (m+1)d+dim S, and the same bound contradicts deficient rank when m≥dim X. Generic finiteness identifies the image dimension with the modular-image dimension.

nodes.title: Frobenius polynomial and reciprocity
nodes.statement: For A/F_q of dimension g, P_A(X)=det(X−Frob_q|V_ℓA) is a monic polynomial in Z[X] of degree 2g, independent of ℓ, with all complex roots of absolute value √q and coefficients satisfying a_(2g−i)=q^(g−i)a_i for 0≤i≤g. Coefficients a_i are indexed in descending powers: P_A=∑_(i=0)^(2g) a_i X^(2g−i), with a_0=1 and a_(2g)=q^g.
proofSteps: Specialize the imported integral, ℓ-independent characteristic polynomial to the q-power Frobenius endomorphism.
Import the Weil absolute-value theorem. The polarization pairing makes Frobenius a q-similitude and gives reciprocal multiplicities; compare coefficients in X^(2g)P_A(q/X)=q^gP_A(X).
The separable isogeny 1−π^r has differential identity, and kernel A(F_(q^r)); its degree is det(1−π^r). Product compatibility follows from the direct sum of Tate representations.

nodes.title: Algebra acting on a Frobenius polynomial block
nodes.statement: Let L/Q_p be unramified of degree a≥1 with arithmetic Frobenius σ, and let m∈Q_p[X] be monic irreducible with m(0)≠0. Put K=Q_p[X]/m and θ=X mod m. On ⊕_(0≤j<a)(L⊗Qp K)U^j define multiplication by U b=(σ⊗1)(b)U and U^a=θ. This defines a K-algebra B of dimension a². If a semilinear bijection F on an L-vector space V satisfies m(F^a)=0, the actions of L, θ↦F^a and U↦F define a B-module structure on V. The coefficient tensor L⊗Q_p K may be étale with several factors; preserve the σ action on all factors.

nodes.title: The splitting principle (Corollary 2.9, Definition 2.10)

nodes.title: The completed Poincaré bundle with connection is the logarithm sheaf (Scheider)
nodes.statement: For 𝒮 = Spec k with k of characteristic zero: the first logarithm sheaf is the extension of 𝒟_𝒜-modules 0 → π^*ℋ → Log^{(1)} → 𝒪_𝒜 → 0 mapping to id_ℋ under the local-to-global sequence 0 → Ext^1_{𝒟_𝒮}(𝒪_𝒮, ℋ) → Ext^1_{𝒟_𝒜}(𝒪_𝒜, π^*ℋ) → Hom_{𝒟_𝒮}(ℋ, ℋ) → 0 (equation (2.7.1)), with a fixed splitting 1^{(1)} : e^*Log^{(1)} ≅ 𝒪_𝒮 ⊕ ℋ; Log^{(n)} = Sym^n Log^{(1)} and 𝓛og = lim Log^{(n)} (Huber–Kings). Theorem 2.36 (Scheider, Theorem 2.3.1): there is a canonical isomorphism (Log^{(1)}, ∇, 1^{(1)}) ≅ (𝒫^{♮(1)}, ∇, 1^{(1)}), hence 𝓛og ≅ 𝒫̂^♮ respecting the sections 1 along e. The proof identifies ker(𝒜^♮(𝒮[M]) → 𝒜^♮(𝒮)) = Lie(𝒜^♮/𝒮) ⊗ M ≅ Hom_k(ℋ, M) (Mazur–Messing (4.1.4); equation (2.7.2)) with Ext^1_{𝒟_𝒜}(𝒪_𝒜, π^*M) through pullback of 𝒫^♮. The base here is Spec k with char k=0; no arbitrary-base version is inferred.
proofSteps: Identify the rigidified first extension with the identity Ext class.

nodes.title: Correct elementary discriminant estimate
nodes.statement: If K=Q(π), π is an integral p-Weil number of degree d, then |D_K|≤|disc minpoly(π)|≤(2√p)^(d(d−1)). nodes.title: Units that are norms modulo norms of units (Lemmermeyer)
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a cyclic extension of number fields of prime degree. There is an exact sequence 1 → Am_st(L/K) → Am(L/K) → (E_K ∩ N_(L/K)L^×)/N_(L/K)E_L → 1, where Am(L/K) ⊂ Cl(L) is the group of ambiguous ideal classes and Am_st(L/K) its subgroup of strongly ambiguous classes. In particular (E_K ∩ N L^×)/N E_L is a subquotient of Cl(L) and its order is at most h(L).
proofSteps: For σ generating Gal(L/K), define ambiguous classes as σ-fixed ideal classes and strongly ambiguous classes as those having a σ-invariant ideal representative.
If a^σ=(α)a, send [a] to Nα modulo norms of units; changing the ideal representative or α does not change the quotient class.
For a unit β=Nα, Hilbert90 for fractional ideals gives (α)=a^(σ−1), so [a] is ambiguous and maps to β. It need not be strongly ambiguous at this step; that word in the printed proof on p.3 is a typo.
If Nα is the norm of a unit η, element Hilbert90 applied to α/η gives a σ-invariant representative of [a]. Thus the kernel is precisely Am_st, and the quotient order is at most h(L).

nodes.statement: For q≥2 and g≥1, the number of monic q-reciprocal integer polynomials (q^gP(X)=X^(2g)P(q/X)) of degree 2g with constant q^g and all roots of absolute value √q is at most (4g+1)^g q^(g(g+1)/4).

For i=1,…,g the power sum has absolute value at most 2g q^(i/2), giving an integer interval with at most (4g+1)q^(i/2) values.
Multiply these interval bounds to obtain (4g+1)^g q^(g(g+1)/4); this counts power sums rather than independently bounding elementary coefficients.
acceptance: For q≥2 and g≥1, the number of monic q-reciprocal integer polynomials (q^gP(X)=X^(2g)P(q/X)) of degree 2g with constant q^g and all roots of absolute value √q is at most (4g+1)^g q^(g(g+1)/4).

nodes.statement: For fixed q, the number of dimension-g F_q-isogeny classes is at most exp((log q)g²/4+O_q(g log g)).

nodes.title: DiPippo–Howe lower bound for isogeny classes
nodes.statement: For every positive integer n and prime power q, the number #O(q,n) of isogeny classes of ordinary n-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q satisfies #O(q,n) > c_4 (c_5 n)^(−2 log 2/log q) (2^n/n!) (r(q) q^(n/2) − n) q^(n(n−1)/4), where c_4 = e^(−3/2), c_5 = 2+√2 and r(q) = φ(q)/q. Hence, with Lemma 2.1 corrected, the logarithm of the number of isogeny classes of g-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q is (1/4)g² log q (1+o(1)) as g→∞, for every fixed q.
proofSteps: Use the compact coefficient map from ordered traces in[−2,2] and the repeated-root boundary criterion (Lemmas2.1.1/2.1.3). The derivative estimate excludes that boundary inside the weighted diamond |b_n|/2+∑_{i<n}|b_i|≤1.

Rectilinear floor bricks give Lemma2.5.2; partitioning orthants with coordinate shifts gives Lemma2.5.3. Apply them to the first n−1 coefficient coordinates with radius1−1/(2n), retaining the explicit small-coordinate subset in Lemma3.2.2.

Count middle coefficients prime to p in[−q^{n/2}/n,q^{n/2}/n]. Proposition3.1.1 uses the ordinary Newton slopes0,1 and Honda multiplicity1 to realize every resulting polynomial. Multiply the two counts to obtain Theorem1.3.

The right side may be negative for small n; retain the source strict inequality rather than taking its logarithm then. For fixed q it becomes positive eventually. Stirling and the explicit prefactor give log#O(q,n)≥(log q)n²/4−O_q(n log n). Combine with the upper bound.
acceptance: For every positive integer n and prime power q, the number #O(q,n) of isogeny classes of ordinary n-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q satisfies #O(q,n) > c_4 (c_5 n)^(−2 log 2/log q) (2^n/n!) (r(q) q^(n/2) − n) q^(n(n−1)/4), where c_4 = e^(−3/2), c_5 = 2+√2 and r(q) = φ(q)/q. Hence, with Lemma 2.1 corrected, the logarithm of the number of isogeny classes of g-dimensional abelian varieties over F_q is (1/4)g² log q (1+o(1)) as g→∞, for every fixed q.

nodes.title: Lemma 5.11, corrected: principal polarizations on E^g
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime that splits in K = Q(√−d) for one of the nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number one (these primes have density 1−2^(−9)). Then there is an elliptic curve E/F_p with End(E) = O_K, and the number of isomorphism classes of principal polarizations on E^g is exp((1/2)g² log g + O_p(g²)). (Printed: exp(g² log g + O(g²)).)

Use the normalized weighted mass over each relevant local genus. Since the imaginary quadratic class number is one, all projective lattices are free. Retain the finitely many norm genera, especially at2; do not suppress them in a single unsupported mass identity.
For fixed K, the logarithm of ∏_{j=1}^g(j−1)! is(1/2)g²log g+O(g²). The powers of2π, discriminants and local factors contribute O_K(g²); the automorphism bound contributes O_K(g log g).

The corrected weighted mass and weighted-to-unweighted comparison yield the two-sided asymptotic. Uniform varying-field residue bounds are not asserted by this fixed-K argument; the primary mass/local-density supplier remains requested.
acceptance: Let p be a prime that splits in K = Q(√−d) for one of the nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number one (these primes have density 1−2^(−9)). nodes.title: Asymptotic exclusion of squarefree nonreal ppavs
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime satisfying the corrected conclusion of Lemma 5.11 (for instance, p splits in one of the nine imaginary quadratic fields of class number one). nodes.title: Reconstruction from integer power sums
nodes.statement: For a monic degree2g integer polynomial satisfying q-reciprocity in descending coefficient convention, its first g power sums determine the entire polynomial. Newton recurrence i·a_i=−∑_(j=1)^i a_(i−j)s_j determines a_i over Q, and reciprocity determines the remaining coefficients.
proofSteps: Factor the polynomial over C, indexing all2g root occurrences, and evaluate the imported MvPolynomial.mul_esymm_eq_sum at these roots.
Use a_i=(−1)^i e_i to obtain i a_i=−∑_{j=1}^i a_{i−j}s_j. The source power sums are integers by this recurrence.
Induct for1≤i≤g over Q, then use a_{2g−i}=q^{g−i}a_i to recover every coefficient. This is an adapter to the existing Newton identity, not a duplicate theorem.
acceptance: For a monic degree2g integer polynomial satisfying q-reciprocity in descending coefficient convention, its first g power sums determine the entire polynomial. Newton recurrence i·a_i=−∑_(j=1)^i a_(i−j)s_j determines a_i over Q, and reciprocity determines the remaining coefficients.

sourceIssues.locator: Compositio156(2020), Lemma9.1/proof, printed pp.2493–2494; PDF pp.26–27; also v6 pp.22–23
sourceIssues.correction: Do not use the unrestricted pullback identity for degeneracy loci across jumping modular fibres. Control the exceptional fibres or prove a stratified global statement; retain this as a gap in the global closedness proof.
sourceIssues.reason: Take a constant abelian surface B, S=Bl₀(B), A=B×S, and X the graph of the blowdown S→B. The modular image is B in a fixed fibre and the map on X has generic relative dimension0. Its exceptional curve E≃P¹ is constant in B; its relative generically special closure over E has relative dimension0<dim E=1, so E⊂X^deg(0). But B in a fixed fibre has empty0-degeneracy locus. Generic finiteness does not imply dimension preservation for every subvariety. This refutes the unrestricted intermediate identity, not the ultimate closedness theorem.
